title: Godparent
text: “Peep!”
My father hands me a pink Filolial chick. As for its gender… it’s a female.
“I heard this before, but is it a good idea to put the eggshell in my shield?”
“That’s right.”
“Thanks. Oh, but it says my level isn’t high enough.”
As expected, being Level 1 puts my father at a disadvantage in many ways. I’ve got to level up my Father soon. After making sure he’s cleaned the eggshells, I take a look at the three Filolials.
“I’ve said this a bunch of times, but what should we name them?”
“Hmm, that’s a tough one…”
“Color schemes are easy enough, but do you have any particular preferences, Motoyasu-kun?”
“Shiro-chan and Lemon are a bit repetitive, aren’t they?”
“Talking about the future? In that case, for white, maybe ‘White’ or ‘Haku’?”
Brilliant! We haven’t named those two yet. That leaves the remaining two. I’ll pick up the pink Filolial-sama and name it myself.
“Pink.”
“That’s way too literal! No way. ‘Pink’ has metaphorical connotations—it’s a bit sad, don’t you think?”
“Hmm… I think a slightly different name would be better, Lord Kitamura.”
“Then please let my Father name it. Pink would be delighted, too.”
“Huh? Hmm… Well, let’s see…”
My Father looks at the Filolial-sama as he ponders. Just like with Filo-tan, it’ll surely be a divine, adorable, and wonderful name.
“The white one looks like snow, so Yuki, and the yellow one looks like a chick, so—”
“Hiyo won’t do.”
I’m pretty sure that was the name of the second Filolial-sama my Father raised. Indirectly, she isn’t *my* angel, but I can’t compromise on that point.
“Um, well, since the character for ‘yellow’ can also be read as ‘Kou,’ maybe ‘Kou’? And for the pink one… ‘Momo’ or maybe ‘Sakura’?”
“In terms of how it rolls off the tongue, wouldn’t ‘Sakura’ be better? It has an exotic… no, wait. It feels similar to the names of Lord Iwatani and the others.”
“Then, according to Father’s naming, it’s Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan!”
The three Filolial-sama chirped cheerfully. Well then, what shall we do? I’ll place the Filolial-sama on both my shoulders and my head.
“Then I’ll go raise the Filolial-sama.”
“Have a safe trip, Motoyasu-kun.”
“As we discussed yesterday, work with the envoy from Siltvelt to carry out the cover operation where you’ll pose as Lord Iwatani, and then make your exit.”
“Understood.”

After talking with Éclair and the others yesterday, we agreed that when leaving this tavern, we’d have our accomplice—who’d be wearing a shield at their waist and a full-body robe—move to a different building before we set out. I hope this confuses the enemy… but it’s better than doing nothing. Then, I tried to move to another shop with my accomplices, including the pig.
“Huh? You there! If you want to pass through here—”

As we were walking down a back alley, a group of shady characters suddenly started picking a fight with us. It’s safe to assume they’re assassins from Melromarc. Even if they aren’t, the fact remains that they’re fools who dared to cross us.
“Shut up! Paralyze Lance!”

Since Father and Éclair asked me to go easy on them as much as possible, I used a skill that inflicts a status ailment and thrust it right into his forehead. It made a satisfying sound, like crunching on a snack.
“Guga—!?”

His whole body must have gone numb—his eyes rolled back, he started foaming at the mouth, and he collapsed. He was twitching uncontrollably, and it looked like he finally realized what a piece of trash he was. This is what happens when you pick a fight with my Father. Seriously, it seems the Three Heroes Church folks just don’t learn their lesson.
“Well then, let’s get going.”

It looked like my ally behind me started swaying slightly, as if on guard, but I can’t say for sure. After seeing my ally off, I left town and set out to help Filolial-sama and the others level up. The deadline is tomorrow night! I’ve got to level up as much as possible by then and pick out a souvenir for my Father!

So, just like before, I headed straight for a remote mountainous area inhabited by dangerous monsters. This time, it seemed there was a nearby region teeming with griffins and dinosaur-type monsters rather than dragons.
“Meteor Thrust X! Brionac X! Gungnir X! Hahahaha! They’re fragile—way too fragile!”
The three Filolial-samas are shadowboxing as if to cheer me on. My top priority is to do my best to make everyone stronger.

But… it brings back memories. It reminds me of when I raised Ku, Marin, and Midori. I arrived at the town below Melromarc Castle in search of Filo-tan, chasing after my Father, only to lose sight of him. And then… just as the stench of pigs was about to make my nose curl, I spotted a monster merchant’s tent. The Monster Merchant back then, hearing me mutter “Filo-tan,” gave me an egg of Filolial-sama for free.

After that, I leveled up alongside Kuu, Marin, and Midori, who had hatched from that egg, and since everyone wanted to race, we became street racers on the mountain pass. We stopped after getting scolded by my Father and the others, but I’ll never forget that sensation of becoming one with the wind.
“Come on, everyone! Let’s get stronger!”

And so, taking Yuki-chan, Kou, and Sakura-chan with me, I continued leveling up in the mountains. Along the way, the monsters started fleeing in droves, but I didn’t care. I’ll chase them to the very depths of the earth and make a bloodbath of them. Well, I’ll try to be somewhat considerate of the environment as I take them down. After all, I’ve got souvenirs for my Father and meals for Filolial-sama to prepare. Still, it only makes sense to keep fighting until I get sleepy.

That’s how our monster-hunting deep in the mountains steadily progressed. While we were at it, we found what looked like a vein of ore, so we picked up some ore as well. Of course, since I’d already put most of it into my spear, I’ll save this for a souvenir for my Father.
But… my luggage is really starting to pile up… I’ll have to get a cart later to haul it all. While I was thinking about that, the sun set in the blink of an eye.

I wonder if my father-in-law and the others are okay? Since there’s no sign of a loop occurring, I suppose we can assume everything went smoothly. Still, I can’t help but worry about my father-in-law.

With those thoughts in mind, I spent the night outdoors with Filolial-sama. By this time, Filolial-sama’s body had already transformed into the shape of a manju. Level 34. Since we’re not returning to Father just yet, that’s about right.
“Piyo…”
“Piyo…”
“Piyo-piyo”
All three of them showed me their cute sleeping faces. Just then… a huge griffin swooped down.
“I hear there’s someone causing trouble in my territory—”
“Brionac X!”

Griffins are also Filolial-sama’s natural enemies—I suppose there are talking griffins out there too, but I’ve never heard of them. It was muttering something under its breath, but I took down the giant griffin without a second thought. It flapped its wings and breathed its last right in the middle of its sentence. That’ll be a feast for tomorrow.
“You’ll wake everyone up. It’s lying dead right there.”
What should we do about the corpse? For now, let’s butcher it and check the drops from the remaining parts.

Oh? A nice-looking piece of armor dropped. Let’s equip it. But what I really like is the Filolial-sama Feather Armor, crafted from the feathers of Her Highness Filolial-sama and her kind! When I get back, I’ll give it to Éclair or my Father.
And so, by the afternoon of the second day, all three of them had reached Level 40. I think that’s a new record for us! Well, the road ahead is turning out to be longer than expected, though.
“Gua?”
“Gua-gua”
“Guaaa!”
They’ve all grown bigger and are chirping energetically. Each one is a delicate white, like snow. A dazzling yellow like flowing lightning. And Sakura, with a soft hue like cherry blossoms.
It’s such a shame about Sakura. If only she had a white base with a cherry blossom hue, she’d be Filo-tan.
“Alright, everyone! Let’s head back to my Father’s place!”
I procured a cart, loaded it with a massive amount of materials, had Filolial-sama transport it, and then I made my way down the mountain.
